items.title: Alvin Alcorn Interview, 1976-01-25
items.q: I knew Louis over 40 years. ... I actually met Louis here in New Orleans when he came to Sublimbore.

ctx.x: The End The End The End Mr. Alcorn, how well did you know Louis Armstrong when he was alive?

I knew Louis over 40 years. I hadn't been a professional musician to him before I met Louis. I'd go back in the old days. I'd say in the late, in the early 30s, or late 20s. I actually met Louis here in New Orleans when he came to Sublimbore. I'd say I had a chance to listen to his records way back when he first started recording the Hot Five. I didn't know Louis when he was a place here. They left and they were in different places, California, Louis and Chicago. Kenora and all of them. That's the area I came to…
Louis Hardin Armstrong played piano in the group. Yeah, King Oliver and all that.

items.title: Alvin Alcorn and Eddie Marrero Interview, 1979-12-04
items.q: Louis. Then we took an oil for sale in the band. That's way back in 1924. ... We played together three times.

ctx.s: Alvin Alcorn (co-interviewee / Marrero family member, NOT interviewer)

ctx.x: I got to him, yeah. Louis. Then we took an oil for sale in the band. That's way back in 1924. Oil for sale, Lawrence, my rival, and me. We played together three times. Treat this and then. So we parted when we got. And the ladies there, they kept on and I stopped. So around four to six I went back. You stopped playing music?
Huh? You stopped playing music for?
